name: fix-cli
contract:
# Contract: release fixes, part D: CLI contract, doctor, Codex schemas and the release path

## Goal

foreman's first release is blocked on findings from three architecture reviews. This unit fixes the user-facing edges: B4, B6, O9, O10, O11, O12, O13, O14, O15 and O16.

- O9 and O10 together: `next:` lines must run as printed in every install mode (compiled binary on `PATH`, the npm launcher `npm/foreman.cjs`, source via `bun run dev`) and keep the invocation's `FOREMAN_HOME`. The npm launcher should tell the binary how it was invoked (the conventional way is an environment variable the launcher sets and `src/config.ts` reads), so `doctor` reports the launcher on `PATH` correctly and `next:` prints `foreman`. Extend the packed-install test in `tests/npm.test.ts` to assert both. You may change `src/config.ts` for that one setting (with its precedence test and `.env.example` entry).
- O11: make the release workflow resumable: publish each platform package only if that exact version isn't already published (verify, then skip), and publish the main package only after all four are confirmed.
- O12, O13 and O15: `doctor` distinguishes a missing daemon from an unresponsive or unreadable one, checks the home directory's ownership and permissions without changing them, and shows hook-refusal details whenever they exist.
- O14: with `--json`, the outdated-daemon notice on stderr is a JSON line.
- B4 and B6: in `src/schemas/codex.ts`, `OtherItem` stops swallowing malformed known item types (allow unfamiliar values where Codex's protocol is open, such as `phase`), and the `ask_orchestrator` input schema is generated from `AskOrchestratorArguments`. Normalisation in `src/core/runs/normalize.ts` belongs to part B; describe any change it needs.
- O16: fix the README example's scope line (``- May change: `src/commands/doctor.ts` ``) and say beside it that scope lines need a leading bullet and backticked paths. Leave the rest of the README to the docs unit that follows.

## Scope

- May change: `src/core/command-output.ts`, `src/core/commands.ts`, `src/commands/runs.ts` (output only; part C owns start flags), `src/core/doctor.ts`, `src/commands/doctor.ts`, `src/schemas/doctor.ts`, `src/schemas/codex.ts`, `src/config.ts` (the launcher setting only), `.env.example`, `npm/`, `scripts/build.ts`, `.github/workflows/release.yml`, `README.md` (the example's scope line only), `tests/commands-*.test.ts`, `tests/npm.test.ts`, `tests/codex-schemas.test.ts`, `tests/config-logging.test.ts` (launcher setting only), `e2e/binary.test.ts` (output and install cases).
- Owned by other units: `src/daemon/`, `src/supervisor/`, `src/core/runs/`, `src/core/managed-worktree.ts`, `src/core/process.ts`, `src/schemas/daemon.ts`.

## How to work

The findings are in `/tmp/scratch` (outside the repo; read it, don't copy it into a tracked file). Each finding has a location, a failure scenario and a proposed fix. The reviewers read the code carefully but could be wrong: confirm each finding against the code before fixing it, and if one is wrong, say so with evidence in the hand-off instead of changing code. If a proposed fix isn't the simplest conventional one, use the better fix and say why.

Read first, in this repo: `AGENTS.md` (all of it, especially Testing and Error handling), `README.md`, `docs/rfcs/0001-foreman.md`, the repo rules (`.claude/rules/effect.md`, `.claude/rules/src/cli.md`, `.claude/rules/src/effect-services.md`, `.claude/rules/src/typescript.md`, `.claude/rules/src/testing.md`, `.claude/rules/src/verification.md`) and the docs each one links, and `docs/guidance/effect/api.md`.

Three other delegates fix other findings in parallel from the same `main` commit, each owning different files (see Scope). Stay inside yours; where a finding needs a file another unit owns, do your side, describe the other side precisely in the hand-off, and the orchestrator will reconcile at merge. Don't ask about this through `ask_orchestrator` unless you're actually blocked.

## Acceptance

Real services, processes, sockets and git repos with the fake app server; no real inference in `tests/` or `e2e/` (AGENTS.md "Testing"). Every finding you fix starts with a test that fails before the fix and passes after, revert-verified; concurrency findings need tests that force the interleaving deterministically (barriers, `TestClock`, fault injection), never sleeps. Run each new or changed test file at least three times, `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run e2e`, and `bun run test` once at the end; report the counts. Don't run `bun run check`. If your area has a real-Codex path, run `FOREMAN_SMOKE=1 FOREMAN_SMOKE_SHORT=1 bun run smoke` once after building (a development check; credits are not a concern).

QA as the first user of what you changed, with the built binary and a temporary `FOREMAN_HOME`, reproducing each blocker's failure scenario before and after where you can. Fix the friction you find (a bug gets a regression test first).

## Do not

- commit or push (leave the changes for review)
- disable a lint rule, weaken a test or add a cast to get green; split an over-complex function into named steps instead
- add features, options, abstractions or mechanisms the findings don't need
- remove any worktree, branch or run data that could hold work, in code or in tests outside temp directories
- add real-Codex tests anywhere `bun run check`, git hooks or CI would run them
- edit `~/.codex` config, hooks, trust or auth, or touch the real `~/.foreman`
- use `ask_orchestrator` for progress reports; use it only when blocked or when a decision is needed
- mention any repository outside this one in a tracked file

## Skills to apply

The `ce` skills and agents come from the Claude Code `claude-essentials` marketplace. Find the newest installed copy with:

```bash
ce=$(ls -d "$HOME"/.claude/plugins/cache/*/ce/*/ | sort -V | tail -1)
```

Read each skill that applies and use it on this task; your hand-off says where it changed what you did.

- `${ce}skills/writing-tests/SKILL.md`: for every test you write, before writing any. Where it and the repo's own testing rules differ, the repo wins. Also read its `references/waiting-typescript.md` for any test that waits on a process, socket, timer or file, and `references/flaky-tests.md` before you call a test done: run each new test file at least three times, and once in the full suite, since this repo has had tests that pass alone and fail under load. The hand-off's Checks section says which tests you wrote, what behaviour each pins down, and which failed before the fix.
- `${ce}skills/architecting-systems/SKILL.md`, with its `references/structure.md`, `coupling.md`, `boundaries.md` and `concurrency.md`: before adding a module.
- `${ce}skills/handling-errors/SKILL.md`: for any error handling you add.
- `${ce}skills/effect/SKILL.md`: for all Effect code.
- `.claude/skills/effect-development/SKILL.md` in this repo.

## Review before hand-off

Once the acceptance checks pass, get one independent code review and fix what it finds. The reviewer is the `ce:code-reviewer` agent (`${ce}agents/code-reviewer.md`) extended by the repo's `.claude/agents/code-reviewer.md` when it exists. This repo's command guard refuses compound shell commands, so run the review as separate simple commands:

1. `mktemp -d` and note the directory it prints, below `<review>`.
2. Write `<review>/prompt.md` with your file-writing tool (not a shell heredoc), containing: the `ce:code-reviewer` agent body without its frontmatter; the repo reviewer's body if that file exists; then these lines: "Skills: <ce>skills/architecting-systems/SKILL.md, <ce>skills/writing-tests/SKILL.md, <ce>skills/handling-errors/SKILL.md. The base branch is main; review the uncommitted work in <worktree>. Your sandbox is read-only, so don't run the tests; the author already ran the checks. The task's contract:" followed by this contract's text, from `/tmp/scratch`.
3. `codex exec --ephemeral --sandbox read-only -m gpt-6.1-sol -c model_reasoning_effort=high -c service_tier=priority -o <review>/review.md - < <review>/prompt.md`

Fix every finding in `review.md`, or say in the hand-off why a finding is wrong. A finding that is a bug gets a regression test in the repo before its fix, revert-verified. Then rerun the acceptance checks. One review pass only.

## Hand-off

You're done when the review's findings are resolved and the acceptance checks pass, or when you're blocked. Leave everything uncommitted and end with this report as your final message; the orchestrator works from it, so be specific and name files and symbols.

1. Summary: what you built, in two or three sentences.
2. Files: each file created or changed, with one line on why.
3. Decisions: choices the contract left open and why you made them; any deviation from the design or contract and the reason; where the skills changed your approach. Name every new mechanism you added and the acceptance test or contract line that needed it.
4. Checks: each command you ran and its result (test counts, not just "passed"), and the QA: what you ran, what you judged and what you changed.
5. Review: the review file's path, each finding in a line, and how you resolved it (fixed, or why not).
6. Look closer at: the places most likely to be wrong.
7. Open: what's left undone or blocked, and the questions you'd ask.

## Deviations found while building

A `thread/start` reply arriving after its timeout is discarded by the client because its request has no waiter left. The run stays `unknown` and becomes `lost` after 5 minutes. No turn was started on that thread, so it does no work.

| Scale within a single process | Producers and consumers scale independently |
| Low operational overhead matters | Fault tolerance and retry logic matter |

Start with in-process async. Move to queues when you need durability, independent scaling, or cross-service decoupling.

**1. Summary**

Implemented the ten scoped findings across CLI continuations, npm launcher identity, doctor diagnostics, Codex schemas, release publishing, and the README example. All changes remain uncommitted; release acceptance is blocked by integration work outside this unit’s scope.

**2. Files**

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `.env.example` | Documents internal `FOREMAN_LAUNCHER`. |
| `.github/workflows/release.yml` | Retains/restores tarballs and uses verified, resumable publishing. |
| `README.md` | Fixes the example’s scope bullet and explains its required format. |
| `npm/foreman.cjs` | Passes launcher identity to the native binary. |
| `npm/release.cjs` — new | Packs artifacts, checks exact-version integrity, and gates main publication on all four platforms. |
| `src/config.ts` | Reads and resolves the launcher setting only. |
| `src/core/command-output.ts` | Preserves absolute home and executable identity; prints executable event continuations. |
| `src/core/commands.ts` | Emits a JSON outdated-daemon notice under `--json`. |
| `src/commands/runs.ts` | Supplies run names for event continuations. |
| `src/core/doctor.ts` | Distinguishes absence from unavailability; inspects home access, ownership, and privacy without mutation. |
| `src/commands/doctor.ts` | Renders new diagnostics and known hook-refusal details. |
| `src/schemas/doctor.ts` | Defines the new diagnostic fields. |
| `src/schemas/codex.ts` | Rejects malformed known items, accepts unfamiliar phases, and generates the tool input schema. |
| `tests/codex-schemas.test.ts` | Schema regressions: 41 total tests. |
| `tests/commands-cli.test.ts` | Continuation and README-scope regressions: 105 total. |
| `tests/commands-doctor.test.ts` | Socket, permissions, ownership, and refusal regressions: 32 total. |
| `tests/commands-release.test.ts` — new | Real packing and publishing failure/retry coverage: 7 tests. |
| `tests/config-logging.test.ts` | Launcher resolution coverage: 35 total. |
| `tests/npm.test.ts` | Packed-install identity, continuations, and failure-safe daemon cleanup: 6 total. |
| `e2e/binary.test.ts` | Compiled, PATH, source, quoted-home, event, and upgrade cases: 9 tests. |

**3. Decisions**

- `FOREMAN_LAUNCHER` identifies the npm entrypoint while daemon startup retains the native executable. Every printed continuation includes the absolute, shell-quoted home (O9/O10).
- Publishing retains exact tarballs and compares registry SHA-512 integrity. Only an explicit registry 404 permits publication; main follows four confirmed platform versions (O11).
- Doctor uses a bounded socket-open probe before Ping because the current daemon client erases connection failure codes (O12).
- No change is needed in `normalize.ts` for unfamiliar phases: its existing agent-message checks and hand-off fallback now accept them.
- The testing skills drove real process/socket coverage and deterministic `TestClock` waits. Error-handling guidance drove explicit unavailable states; architecture guidance kept release logic in one Node helper. Effect and writing guidance informed schema generation and diagnostics.

**4. Checks**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Six changed Vitest files together | **226 passed** after review fixes. Every changed test file passed at least three runs/file-set runs. |
| `bun run test:unit tests/npm.test.ts` | **6 passed**, including three post-fix runs. |
| `bun run lint` | Passed: **122 files**. |
| `bun run typecheck` | Passed. |
| `bun run e2e` | **9 passed**, including four runs of the final cases and a post-review run. |
| `bun run test` | Final: **786 passed, 20 failed / 806**, all failures in untouched `tests/supervisor-integration.test.ts`. Earlier runs had 19 failures. |
| `FOREMAN_SMOKE=1 FOREMAN_SMOKE_SHORT=1 bun run smoke` | **9 passed, 7 failed**; failures reject the new home-assignment prefix in `smoke/helpers.ts`. |
| `git diff --check` | Passed. |

Revert verification reproduced 46 unit regression failures, two compiled/PATH continuation failures, the JSON-notice failure, and the review cleanup failure. Logs: [baseline regressions](/tmp/foreman-revert-0Nu7i1/unit.log), [cleanup regression](/tmp/foreman-review-vrUWux/cleanup-revert.log).

Manual QA verified binary/source doctor output, unchanged directory permissions, and printed commands executed from another directory with a conflicting home. Real-Codex delegation, question/answer, and hook-refusal cases passed. No publication was attempted. `bun run check` was not run.

**5. Review**

[Independent review](/tmp/foreman-review-vrUWux/review.md) found one issue: failed npm assertions could leave detached daemons running while their homes were deleted.

Fixed with `withDaemonHomes`, tracked cleanup, PID-exit verification, and guarded directory removal. The regression starts both possible homes, forces an assertion failure, and confirms both processes exit. Revert-verified; no second review pass was run.

**6. Look closer at**

- Reconcile doctor’s additional socket probe with the daemon unit’s revised error contract.
- The GitHub artifact restore/upload path was inspected and locally exercised through packing/publishing tests; it has not run in Actions.
- Final full-suite log: [806-test run](/tmp/foreman-review-vrUWux/final-full-test.log).

**7. Open**

Acceptance needs these out-of-scope changes:

- `tests/supervisor-integration.test.ts`: update continuation parsing and JSON upgrade-notice expectations.
- `src/supervisor/notifications.ts`: preserve hook enforcement using a validated minimal item envelope before detailed decoding. Strict B4 decoding now bypasses the guard for malformed `commandExecution` starts. Preserve the malformed-payload tests at lines 2218 and 2485.
- `smoke/helpers.ts:nextCommand`: consume and validate the leading `FOREMAN_HOME=…` assignment.
- Investigate the additional final-run recovery failure at `tests/supervisor-integration.test.ts:1381`: expected the last event to be `StateChanged/lost`, received `QuestionResolved`. It passed in the previous two full runs.

No design questions remain.
